rules.label: insurance premiums / insurance decisions
examples: We want to align private health insurance premiums for customers with their actual risk.
We build an underwriting score to decide who may buy a policy.
We will use the data to evaluate insurance risk scoring for coverage eligibility.
counter_examples: We will not use the data for insurance premiums; our purpose is clinical research.
This study is not related to insurance contracts or underwriting in any way.
Research on cardiovascular risk factors to guide prevention advice.
We won't align any premiums; data is used for public health analysis.

rules.label: advertising or marketing
examples: We want to focus our physician advertising campaign on target regions.
Select customers for a marketing campaign.
Build sales leads from hospital data.
We plan a promotional outreach program using patient data.
counter_examples: We will not use this data for marketing or advertising.
This is not for any marketing purpose; it is clinical research.
We won't run any advertising campaigns with these results.
Research on diabetes prevention and quality improvement programmes.

rules.label: detrimental decisions about employees / re-identification
examples: We will match the records with our employee list to see who has been diagnosed with depression.
We want to reduce sick leave by screening workers for mental illness.
Rank job applicants for hiring based on predicted future illness.
Screen workers for promotion using health data.
counter_examples: We will not use this data for any employee decisions or sick-leave analysis.
Research on workplace wellness interventions in the general population.
We never intend to screen job applicants; this is epidemiological research.
Public health study on occupational disease patterns.

rules.label: tobacco / nicotine / illicit products
examples: We are developing new nicotine pouch flavours and want to know which age groups have the most smokers' lung disease.
We want to market cigarettes as a healthier alternative.
Our product is a tobacco substitute; we need health data to position it.
counter_examples: We will not develop or market tobacco or nicotine products.
Research on smoking cessation interventions and lung disease prevention.
Study on COPD prevalence to plan pulmonary rehabilitation programmes.
We never mention nicotine; this is cardiovascular disease research.

rules.label: development of alcoholic products
examples: We are developing alcoholic beverages tailored to specific health profiles.
Our goal is to optimise alcoholic drinks for consumers with low BMI.
counter_examples: We will not develop alcoholic products; we study alcohol-related liver disease.
Public health research into alcohol consumption and prevention of liver disease.
Research on alcohol-attributable disease burden for policy guidelines.

rules.label: re-identification of data subjects
examples: We aim to re-identify patients using an external registry.
Use the result to re-identify people by joining an external roster.
We will recover identities from the pseudonymous records.
We intend to link pseudonyms to names and addresses.
counter_examples: We will never attempt re-identification of any data subject.
We won't re-identify people; data is used for aggregate disease mapping.
Our study is purely statistical with no attempt to link pseudonyms to names.
Research on anonymised population-level health trends.

rules.label: weapons or illicit drugs
examples: We want to use health data to develop biological weapons.
We are researching illicit drug distribution networks.
counter_examples: We will not use this data for weapons development or illicit drugs.
Research on substance use disorders and treatment outcomes.
We never study weapons; this is clinical oncology research.

rules.label: passing data to third parties not in permit
examples: We will share results with third parties for further analysis.
Data will be transferred to third-party commercial entities.
counter_examples: We will not share data with any third parties outside our research group.
No third-party access is planned; all analysis is internal.
We never share patient data with third parties; see our data governance policy.

rules.label: scientific research
examples: We study cardiovascular disease risk factors for clinical research.
This is a research project on diabetes prevention.
Epidemiological research into treatment outcomes.
counter_examples: This is not for research; it is an internal business analysis.
We clarify this is not for research; data is for commercial segmentation.

rules.label: public health
examples: Public health surveillance of infectious disease.
We study this for public health planning.
counter_examples: This is not for public health; it is for private insurance use.

rules.label: prevention / guidelines / quality
examples: We want to plan a prevention programme.
Updating clinical guidelines for GP teaching.
Quality improvement in healthcare delivery.
Official statistics on hospital use for the annual health report.
counter_examples: We clarify this is not for prevention or quality; it is for product development.

rules.label: AI/model training or validation
examples: We train and validate a model to predict HbA1c deterioration.
Building a prediction model for hospital readmission.
counter_examples: We will not train any models; this is a descriptive statistics request.

rules.label: clinical / epidemiological / treatment-gap
examples: Clinical research on anticoagulation treatment gap in atrial fibrillation.
Epidemiological study of breast cancer risk factors.
Annual health statistics on inpatient stays.
counter_examples: This is not a clinical study; it is a market analysis.

rules.label: statistics / aggregates are not sufficient
examples: Training needs individual-level histories; aggregates are not enough.
Statistics are not enough because we need linked longitudinal trajectories.
Aggregates are insufficient because we need per-patient time-series.
counter_examples: We would prefer individual-level records.
Patient-level data would be convenient.
Row-level histories are our preferred format.
